stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most vaccines teach the immune system to recognize a threat by exposing it to a weakened or inactivated version of the entire pathogen, so the body encounters dozens of the microbe's surface proteins at once. Subunit vaccines, ______ contain only a single purified protein from the pathogen, which is why they usually need an added ingredient called an adjuvant to provoke a strong enough response.
explanation: There are two subjects here: most vaccines, which present the whole pathogen and many proteins, and subunit vaccines, which present a single protein. The subjects differ and the attribute flips from many to one. That is a comparison-contrast relationship, so you need 'by contrast.'

A.why: You saw a specific kind of vaccine come after a general statement and took it as an illustration. Subunit vaccines go against the tendency described in the first sentence, because they do not use the whole pathogen. A case that breaks the general claim cannot be an example of it.

B.why: 'Similarly' needs the two subjects to share an attribute. A single purified protein is the opposite of 'dozens of surface proteins,' so the two sentences point in different directions.

D.why: You read a cause-and-effect link that the text does not contain. Whole-pathogen vaccines do not cause subunit vaccines to hold a single protein. The two are simply set side by side as different approaches.

subtype_name: Two things set side by side (By contrast / Conversely)

rated_why: identifies straightforward contrast between vaccine-delivery methods

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most planned towns built in the mid-twentieth century separated land uses, zoning homes far from shops and workplaces so that residents had to drive to run almost any errand. explanation: The first sentence gives the usual pattern: planned towns built so that residents had to drive. Veldmoor is a planned town from the same era, but it was built so that residents could cycle to daily destinations. It reverses the usual pattern, so 'conversely' is the logical transition.

B.why: You chose an example word because one particular town follows a general claim about planned towns. Check whether the case agrees with the claim first. Veldmoor was designed around cycling rather than driving, so it goes against the tendency instead of illustrating it.

C.why: 'In other words' introduces a restatement of the same idea in different terms. The second sentence describes a different town with the opposite design, not a rewording of the first sentence.

D.why: Nothing in the passage says that other towns' car-centered zoning caused Veldmoor's cycle-path layout. You supplied a cause the text never states.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: P waves, the fastest seismic waves an earthquake produces, compress and stretch rock along their direction of travel and can pass through both the solid and the liquid layers of Earth's interior. S waves, ______ shake rock perpendicular to their direction of travel and cannot cross liquid at all. Their disappearance beyond a certain distance from an earthquake gave seismologists early evidence that Earth's outer core is molten.
explanation: The two sentences use the same frame for two kinds of wave. P waves move along the direction of travel and pass through liquid. S waves move perpendicular to it and cannot pass through liquid. The subjects differ and the key attribute flips, so 'in contrast' is correct.

A.why: 'Similarly' only works if S waves share the attribute given for P waves. P waves cross liquid and S waves cannot, so the two are opposites, not parallels.

B.why: S waves are not a sample of P waves or of anything the first sentence describes. They are a second, separate category with the opposite behavior. You treated a specific item as an illustration without checking whether it agrees with what came before.

C.why: P waves' ability to cross liquid does not make S waves move perpendicular or stop at liquid. The passage compares two wave types. It does not describe one causing the other.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Coaches in most endurance sports have their athletes taper, sharply cutting training volume in the final weeks before a race, because rested muscles typically produce faster times. Among the ultramarathon runners tracked by physiologist Lena Okafor, ______ those who tapered for more than ten days finished slower than those who kept training, apparently because very long races reward resistance to fatigue more than fresh legs.
explanation: The first sentence states a general rule: tapering usually produces faster times. Among Okafor's ultramarathoners, a long taper produced slower times. The specific case breaks the rule, so you need a contrast word, 'by contrast.'

A.why: This is the classic trap. A specific group of runners follows a general claim, so it looks like an example. But those runners got slower after tapering, which contradicts the claim that tapering produces faster times. An example has to agree with what it illustrates.

C.why: 'Thus' says the second sentence follows from the first. Slower times after tapering do not follow from a rule that tapering speeds athletes up. They cut against it.

D.why: 'Furthermore' adds a point in the same direction. Try the 'and also' test: 'Tapering produces faster times, and also tapering produced slower times' sounds wrong because the second idea contradicts the first.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Baroque composers typically left ornamentation to the performer, writing only a bare melodic line and trusting skilled players to add trills and flourishes of their own. Johann Sebastian Bach, ______ wrote out many of his ornaments note by note, a habit that the critic Johann Adolph Scheibe attacked in 1737 for burying the natural beauty of a melody under too much detail.
explanation: The first sentence describes what Baroque composers usually did: leave ornaments to the performer. Bach did the reverse and wrote them out himself. Scheibe's criticism confirms that this was unusual. Because Bach's practice goes against the general tendency, 'by contrast' is correct.

B.why: 'Similarly' would mean Bach also left ornaments to performers. Writing them out note by note is the opposite attribute, so an addition word misstates the relationship.

D.why: Other composers' habit of leaving ornaments to performers did not cause Bach to write his out. You read a consequence into two practices that are only being compared.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The Mercator projection preserves the angles between lines on a map, which made it invaluable to navigators plotting a constant compass heading, but it enlarges landmasses more and more the farther they lie from the equator. Equal-area projections such as the Gall-Peters, ______ keep the relative sizes of landmasses accurate while distorting their shapes, stretching Africa and South America into noticeably elongated forms.
explanation: There are two subjects: the Mercator projection and equal-area projections. Mercator keeps shapes and angles but distorts size. Equal-area projections keep size but distort shape. The trade-off is reversed, so 'conversely' is the logical transition.

B.why: The phrase 'such as the Gall-Peters' already names an example within the second sentence, and that may have pulled you toward an example transition. But the transition has to link the two sentences, and equal-area projections are not an example of the Mercator projection. They make the opposite trade-off.

C.why: 'In addition' adds another point in the same direction. Here the second projection keeps exactly what the first one distorts and distorts what the first one keeps. That is an opposition, not an addition.

D.why: 'Hence' presents the second sentence as a result of the first. The Mercator projection's features do not produce the Gall-Peters projection's features. The passage sets two separate designs side by side.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most field crops cannot reach high yields without large applications of nitrogen fertilizer, whether synthetic or from manure, because they draw nitrogen from the soil faster than natural processes replace it. Soybeans, ______ supply much of their own nitrogen: bacteria living in small nodules on their roots convert nitrogen from the air into a form the plant can absorb, so farmers often apply little or none.
explanation: The first sentence makes a general claim: most field crops need heavy nitrogen fertilizer. Soybeans are a field crop that largely does not, because root bacteria supply the nitrogen. The specific case breaks the general pattern, so 'by contrast' is correct.

B.why: Other crops' dependence on fertilizer does not cause soybeans to make their own nitrogen. The root bacteria cause that. 'As a result' invents a causal link the passage never draws.

C.why: 'Likewise' would mean soybeans also depend on added nitrogen. The passage says the opposite, so a same-direction word does not fit.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most suspension bridges built in the early twentieth century relied on stiffening trusses: deep steel frameworks hung beneath the deck to keep it from twisting in strong wind. Engineers regarded these trusses as costly but indispensable. The Whitmore Span, completed in 1931, ______ was designed with a plate girder only a few feet deep, a choice that saved tons of steel and gave the deck a strikingly slender profile.
explanation: Start by naming each subject and what is said about it. The first subject is most early twentieth-century suspension bridges, which used deep stiffening trusses. The second is the Whitmore Span, which used a shallow girder instead. The two subjects are different, and the attribute flips from deep truss to shallow girder, so the relationship is a contrast. 'By contrast' is the comparison-contrast word that sets the Whitmore Span against the general practice.

A.why: You saw one specific bridge after a statement about most bridges and took it as an example. An example has to agree with the general claim. The Whitmore Span does the opposite of what most bridges did, so it cannot illustrate the trend.

B.why: 'Similarly' needs both subjects to share the same attribute. The other bridges used deep trusses and the Whitmore Span used a shallow girder, so the two are not alike.

D.why: 'Therefore' says the second sentence follows as a result of the first. Engineers thinking trusses were indispensable cannot be the reason a bridge left them out. If anything, the design went against that belief.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Through much of the eighteenth century, the silk workshops of Lyon bought their patterns from independent designers, who often sold a single drawing to several competing shops at once. As a result, nearly identical brocades could appear in rival showrooms within the same season. The workshop run by Héloïse Varenne, ______ kept a staff of salaried draftsmen and allowed no design to leave its premises.
explanation: Name the two subjects and their attributes. Most Lyon workshops bought shared patterns from outside designers. Varenne's workshop made its own patterns in-house and kept them private. C.why: A single named workshop follows a statement about most workshops, so 'for instance' is tempting. But an instance has to show the general pattern, and Varenne's workshop breaks it. A specific case that goes against the tendency is a contrast, not an example.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most vaccines in routine use protect the body by prompting it to make antibodies, proteins that circulate in the blood and neutralize a pathogen before it can enter cells. The measles vaccine works this way, and a simple blood test of antibody levels is a reliable gauge of how well a person is protected. The shingles vaccine, ______ appears to work chiefly by strengthening T cells, which destroy cells that are already infected, so antibody counts say little about whether its protection will hold.
explanation: Name each subject and what is said about it. The measles vaccine works through antibodies, and antibody tests measure its protection. The shingles vaccine works mainly through T cells, and antibody tests tell you little. Two different vaccines are described in the same frame with the key attribute reversed, so you need a word for a difference between two cases. 'By contrast' is that word.

A.why: You saw one specific vaccine after a general claim about 'most vaccines' and took it as an example. But the shingles vaccine doesn't work the way most vaccines do. It's an exception, and an exception can't illustrate the rule it breaks.

C.why: You read the shingles sentence as a result of the measles sentence. How the measles vaccine works doesn't cause the shingles vaccine to work differently. The two facts are compared, and neither one causes the other.

D.why: 'Similarly' needs both vaccines to share the attribute being described. The passage says the opposite: one relies on antibodies and the other on T cells.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Engineers designing a long-span bridge usually choose between two structural systems. In a suspension bridge, the deck hangs from vertical cables attached to two main cables, which drape over the towers and must be anchored in massive blocks of concrete or bedrock at each end of the span. In a cable-stayed bridge, ______ cables run in straight lines from the towers directly to the deck, so the structure needs no anchorages at its ends at all.
explanation: The first sentence names two systems, and the next two sentences describe each one in the same frame: 'In a ___ bridge, the deck/cables...'. The attribute flips. The suspension bridge must be anchored at its ends, and the cable-stayed bridge needs no end anchorages. Two parallel cases with opposite attributes call for a contrast word, so 'conversely' is right.

A.why: 'Two structural systems' looks like an umbrella term with members to list, so 'for example' felt natural. But the sentence doesn't sample a group to support a claim. It sets the second system against the first, and the point is how they differ.

B.why: 'As a result' would mean the suspension bridge's design causes the cable-stayed bridge's design. Nothing in the passage connects them that way. They are two separate options being compared.

D.why: 'Likewise' says the cable-stayed bridge shares the suspension bridge's feature. On the key point, anchorage, the passage says it doesn't: one needs end anchorages and the other needs none.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Archaeologists long assumed that large stone monuments appeared only after people had settled into farming villages, since only farmers, the reasoning went, could store enough surplus food to feed a crew of builders. Most early monumental sites in the region fit this pattern, rising centuries after the first cultivated grain. The ring of carved pillars at Kessar Hill, ______ was raised by groups who still lived entirely by hunting animals and gathering wild plants.
explanation: The second sentence gives the general pattern: most monumental sites were built by farmers. The blank sentence gives one specific site, Kessar Hill, that was built by hunter-gatherers. That reverses the pattern. A site that breaks the tendency is set against it, not used to illustrate it, so 'by contrast' is the logical choice.

A.why: A specific site follows a general claim, so you reached for 'for instance'. But check whether the case agrees with the claim. Kessar Hill was built by people who did not farm, so it goes against the pattern rather than illustrating it.

B.why: Try putting 'and also' between the sentences. 'Most sites came after farming, and also this site was built by hunter-gatherers' doesn't work. The second fact undercuts the first rather than adding to it.

C.why: 'Consequently' would make Kessar Hill's hunter-gatherer builders a result of the farming pattern. The pattern can't cause its own exception. The relationship is opposition, not cause and effect.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Leaves settle quickly into the fine mud of lake beds, so they make up most of the plant fossils that paleobotanists recover. Trunks and branches, by comparison, usually rot or break apart before they can be buried. A recently excavated site in central Montana, ______ has yielded more than forty upright fossil trunks and only a handful of leaf impressions, probably because a sudden fall of volcanic ash buried the standing trees where they grew.
explanation: Start with the two cases. The first sentences describe fossil sites in general: mostly leaves, few trunks. The Montana site shows the reverse: many trunks, almost no leaves. Two cases with the attribute flipped is a contrast, so "by contrast" is the right transition.

B.why: You saw one specific site after a general claim and reached for an example word. An example has to agree with the claim it illustrates. This site goes against the usual pattern, so it can't serve as an example of it.

C.why: "Likewise" needs both cases to share the same attribute. The usual site is mostly leaves and the Montana site is mostly trunks, so the attributes are opposite.

D.why: "Therefore" says the Montana finding follows from the earlier sentences. Nothing about leaves settling in mud would cause a site to be full of trunks. The passage gives a separate cause, the ashfall.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Hydrologists distinguish two main kinds of aquifer. In an unconfined aquifer, water seeps straight down through the soil above, so the water table rises and falls within days of local rainfall. A confined aquifer, ______ is sealed beneath a layer of clay or dense rock, and its water level may reflect rain that fell many kilometers away, sometimes decades earlier.
explanation: Each sentence names one kind of aquifer and says how its water level responds. The unconfined aquifer is open to the surface and reacts quickly to local rain. The confined aquifer is sealed off and reacts to distant, much older rain. These are two parallel categories with opposite attributes, so "conversely" fits.

A.why: The first sentence names a group ("two main kinds"), and you took the sentence about one kind as an example. But the blank sits in the second of two parallel descriptions. Its job is to set the confined aquifer against the unconfined one, not to illustrate the general statement.

B.why: "In addition" just adds another point in the same direction. Try putting "and also" between the sentences: the confined aquifer is the opposite of the unconfined one, not more of the same, so it sounds wrong.

D.why: "As a result" means the confined aquifer's features are caused by how the unconfined aquifer behaves. They are two separate systems, and neither one causes the other.

stem: Which choice does NOT complete the text with a logical transition?
stimulus: Before synthetic dyes appeared in the 1850s, most plant-based dyes used by European weavers were fugitive: washing and sunlight stripped their color within a few years, so garments had to be redyed or thrown away. Indigo, ______ bonded so firmly to wool and linen fibers that blue cloth often outlasted the garments cut from it, which helps explain why so many surviving folk costumes from the period are blue.
explanation: The first sentence makes a general claim: most plant dyes faded quickly. The second sentence picks out one dye, indigo, and says the opposite about it, because its color lasted. Indigo is a plant dye, so it looks like a member of the group, but it goes against the group's tendency instead of showing it. That makes the relationship a contrast. 'For example' would present indigo as a sample of fading dyes, which reverses what the passage says. So 'for example' is the choice that does NOT work.

A.why: 'By contrast' works, because indigo's lasting color is the opposite of the fading the first sentence describes. If you rejected it, you probably saw a specific item following a general category and decided the sentence had to be an example. Check whether the case agrees with the general claim before you call it an example.

C.why: 'However' works, because the second sentence reverses the first. Most dyes faded, but indigo held. If you ruled it out, you may have thought 'however' can't sit in the middle of a sentence. It can, as long as commas set it off, as they do here.

D.why: 'On the other hand' works, because it sets indigo's lasting color against the fading of the other dyes. If you rejected it, you probably read indigo as one instance of the dyes the first sentence describes, which is the example trap.

stem: Which choice does NOT complete the text with a logical transition?
stimulus: Paleobotanists reconstructing ancient forests often rely on two kinds of plant fossils. Pollen grains, protected by tough outer walls of a polymer called sporopollenin, survive in lake sediments for millions of years and can be counted by the thousand from a single core. Leaves, ______ decay within weeks unless they are buried quickly in fine mud, so a fossil leaf bed records only a brief and unusual moment of preservation.
explanation: The passage names two kinds of fossils and gives each one the same attribute, how well it survives, with the values flipped. Pollen lasts for millions of years. Leaves decay within weeks. Different subjects with opposite attributes call for a contrast word. 'Likewise' needs the two subjects to share the same attribute, and these two don't. So 'likewise' is the choice that does NOT work.

A.why: 'Conversely' works, because the leaves have the reverse of the pollen's trait: fragile instead of durable. If you rejected it, you may have thought 'conversely' only fits a reversed cause and effect. On this test it also fits two parallel cases whose attributes flip.

B.why: 'On the other hand' works, because it sets the second of the 'two kinds' of fossils against the first. If you ruled it out, you may have noticed that both sentences are about fossils and treated that shared topic as a shared attribute. Compare what is said about each subject, not just what the subjects are.

D.why: 'By contrast' works, because the leaves decay quickly while the pollen survives. If you rejected it, you probably read the second sentence as just continuing the list of fossil types. The list continues, but what it says about leaves reverses what it said about pollen.

stem: Which choice does NOT complete the text with a logical transition?
stimulus: In a drought trial at a Kansas research station, agronomists withheld irrigation from 40 wheat varieties during flowering, the stage at which the plants are most sensitive to water stress. Most of the varieties lost roughly half their expected grain yield. A traditional landrace collected from farms in northern Ethiopia, ______ lost less than a tenth, a result the team attributes to the variety's unusually deep roots.
explanation: The sentence before the blank gives a general result: most varieties lost about half their yield. The sentence with the blank takes one variety from the trial and reports the opposite, since it lost less than a tenth. A single case that breaks the trend is a contrast, not an illustration. 'For example' would make the Ethiopian landrace a typical case of heavy loss, which the numbers contradict. So 'for example' is the choice that does NOT work.

A.why: 'By contrast' works, because the landrace's small loss is set against the heavy losses of most varieties. If you rejected it, you probably saw one variety singled out after a statement about 'most of the varieties' and assumed it had to be an example. Compare the numbers first: less than a tenth is the opposite of roughly half.

B.why: 'However' works, because the landrace's result runs against the general one. If you ruled it out, you may have thought 'however' has to start a sentence. Set off by commas after the subject, it is standard and logical.

C.why: 'Though' works. Placed mid-sentence and set off by commas, it means 'however', and it marks the landrace as the exception. If you rejected it, you may have been reading it as the conjunction 'although', which would need a second clause. Here it is a contrast adverb.
